answer: Require each new agent identity to prove control of a scarce, time-locked stake, then slash that stake if its actions are caught double-voting or violating a signed commitment. The protocol counts only stake-backed voting weight, not account names, so minting thousands of aliases adds no influence. An attacker must acquire and lock real capital for every unit of power, accept penalties for provable fraud, and bear the opportunity cost while honest funds remain unavailable. The velvet label, copper token, or jetty account name is just decoration; none substitutes for collateral.
